facts.about: Dixon Technologies (India) Limited, incorporated in 1993 , is a Electronic Manufacturing Services (EMS) company with operations in the electronic products vertical such as consumer electronics, lighting, home appliance, closed-circuit television cameras (CCTVs), and mobile phones. It also undertakes reverse logistics operations. Besides, it manufactures security surveillance equipment, wearables & audibles, AC-PCBs. Recently, it has entered a JV with Imagine Marketing Private Limited for designing and manufacturing wireless audio solutions in India.

business.summary: Dixon Technologies (India) Limited is engaged in the manufacturing of consumer electronics, telecom, and networking products, including smartphones, routers, and set-top boxes, operating through various subsidiaries and joint ventures.

scorecard.promised: Targeting 33-34 million units for FY27, including H2 outlook.
scorecard.delivered: Pending; current run-rate suggests a potential shortfall versus the 33-34 million target.
scorecard.evidence: Management guided 33-34m units in Q2 FY27, but Q4 FY26 guidance was only 7-7.5m units per quarter.

scorecard.promised: Expected to exceed INR 4,000 crores in FY27.
scorecard.delivered: Pending; long-term target revised upward to INR 15,000-20,000 crores over two years.
scorecard.evidence: Initial FY27 target was >INR 4,000cr (c2g1), later raised to INR 15,000cr+ horizon (c0g2).

scorecard.promised: Maintain margins between 2.8% to 3.2% for the mobile phone business.
scorecard.delivered: Delivered 2.7% consolidated margin in Sep 2026, reflecting compression.
scorecard.evidence: Consolidated margins fell from 3.9% in Mar 2026 to 2.7% in Sep 2026.

scorecard.promised: Targeting INR 6,700 crores to INR 7,000 crores for FY27.
scorecard.delivered: Revised down from earlier target of INR 7,500-8,000 crores.
scorecard.evidence: Guidance shifted from INR 7.5k-8k cr (c2g2) down to INR 6.7k-7k cr (c1g2).

scorecard.promised: INR 1,100-1,200 crores for FY26 and similar run rate for FY27.
scorecard.delivered: On track with INR 885 crores in Capital Work in Progress as of Sep 2026.
scorecard.evidence: CWIP of INR 885cr and management commitment to INR 1,200cr close (c0g5).

narrative.scoreline: Management is successfully scaling top-line volumes but faces significant credibility hurdles as margins compress and specific segment revenue targets are revised downward.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Margins were impacted by Mobile PLI 1 expiration and memory price inflation.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Consolidated margins dropped from 3.9% in Mar 2026 to 2.7% in Sep 2026.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Working capital increase is temporary and 80-85% will release by March.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Cash conversion cycle is -7 days, but receivables and payables have surged per analyst pushback.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Smartphone input costs are a pass-through with no impact on margins.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Despite pass-through claims, consolidated margins have trended lower as revenue scaled.

bull: Revenue grew 46.7% YoY in Sep 2026, maintaining strong top-line momentum.
Excellent cash generation with 5-year operating cash flow at 122% of PAT.
Aggressive expansion into IT hardware with a target of INR 15,000cr+ revenue.
bear: Operating margins have compressed significantly to 2.7% following Mobile PLI 1 expiry.
Telecom revenue guidance was revised downward from INR 8,000cr to INR 7,000cr.
High memory prices and ASP increases are softening volume growth expectations.
watch: Release of 80-85% blocked working capital by March 2027.
Commencement of Vivo JV operations in Q3 FY27.
Margin recovery toward 3% level as component integration scales.

claims.claim: Margins were impacted by mobile PLI 1 expiration, memory price inflation, and input cost pass-through lags.
claims.quote: Margins during the quarter were impacted on expiration of mobile PLI 1 scheme along with elevated global memory prices due to rapid expansion of AI infrastructure.

claims.claim: Transitioning to global category under IT PLI 2 with increased capex to INR 500 crores.
claims.quote: we are now transitioning from hybrid category with INR 250 crores of CAPEX commitment to global category with INR 500 crores CAPEX requirement under IT PLI 2

claims.claim: Working capital is elevated due to strategic memory inventory and pending PLI receivables, 80-85% should release by March.
claims.quote: we feel that out of this large part of money which is blocked at the money working capital, we feel that almost 80-85% of that will get released before March.

claims.claim: Margins were compressed due to Mobile PLI 1 expiry and higher input costs passed through to selling prices.
claims.quote: Operating margin for the quarter reflected temporary compression on account of expiry of Mobile PLI 1 in March '26 and from increased selling prices driven by elevated input costs.

claims.claim: Working capital increase was a temporary phenomenon due to strategic inventory accumulation and timing of creditor payments.
claims.quote: It's a combination of these three things... strategic inventories because there were supply chain challenges... and also we had some extra cash if you see lying at the end of March.

claims.claim: The scheme is well-curated to support both volume growth and deeper value addition through localization.
claims.quote: So, Aditya, we feel that it's a very well-curated scheme. It's a combination of both elements that you mentioned. One is on boosting volumes... and the second is on more and more localization.

claims.claim: Excluding Vivo, we expect volumes to be similar to last year due to memory price inflation.
claims.quote: We feel that the overall volumes without Vivo is going to be almost similar, okay? Because there is an overall decline due to increase in the memory prices and the ASP going up significantly.

claims.claim: Margins will be under pressure due to PLI expiry, but will expand 40-50 bps once components are deployed.
claims.quote: So the margin profile will be slightly under pressure this year because the PLI has gone off, and there is a lag in the margin accretion happening due to component foray. But finally, when the component play is completely deployed, there will be a margin expansion from last year's number by almost 40 bps, 50 bps.

claims.claim: Display business is expected to reach INR5,500-6,000 crores revenue with double-digit margins at scale.
claims.quote: In the final picture of this business, the revenue target, once we start achieving 80% to 90% of the capacity utilization, the revenue generation is going to be almost INR5,500 crores to INR6,000 crores with a double-digit margin.

claims.claim: Backward integration into components will drive margin expansion in FY27-28.
claims.quote: But '27-'28, we are absolutely confident that there should be a decent margin expansion largely on account of component play.

claims.claim: Smartphone input costs are a pass-through for us, so there is no impact on our margins.
claims.quote: As far as the unit economics is concerned, for us, it's a pass-through. For us, there is no impact as far as the value chain and impact on the margins is concerned.

claims.claim: We remain committed to our aggressive growth target of over INR1 lakh crore in 3-4 years.
claims.quote: We are committed to an aggressive growth for Dixon. We feel confident about it. We feel committed to that.

risks.text: Material related party transactions require shareholder approval if they exceed specified materiality thresholds.
Contingent liabilities are disclosed when an outflow of resources is possible but not probable.
Impairment testing of investments and goodwill involves significant management judgment and estimation.
